description: SF-038 AWS-managed component catalog mapped to SuiFleet native equivalents, scoped adapters (implementation tickets SF-057 to SF-063) and roadmap gaps (SF-064). Linux x86_64/aarch64/arm is the initial prototype phase. Per-adapter runtime receipts distinguish local execution from reference models. Live AWS acceptance is unauthorized and unrun. See docs/GREENGRASS_MANAGED_COMPONENTS.md.

reference.catalog: AWS-provided components (36 rows) and machine learning components (11 rows) tables, Greengrass V2 developer guide
reference.version_policy: reference_version is the latest version listed in the component's AWS changelog on the checked date and is recorded only for components whose page was read. An adapter implementation ticket must re-check and pin the exact AWS version it matches before implementation.

dispositions.native: A SuiFleet subsystem owned by the listed tickets provides the functional equivalent. No AWS interface is reproduced.
dispositions.native-component: No SuiFleet runtime change. The operator packages equivalent open software as an ordinary native component.
dispositions.adapter: A scoped SuiFleet adapter that talks to the AWS service or emulates its local interface, owned by the adapter's implementation_ticket. Not implemented until that ticket runs its runtime tests.
dispositions.roadmap: Not provided in the initial Linux prototype phase. Missing functional work tracked by SF-064, which splits it into concrete tickets before implementation; not an approved permanent exclusion. native_equivalent is an interim workaround, not AWS API or recipe compatibility.
dispositions.not-applicable: Has no meaning for SuiFleet, including AWS services AWS has discontinued.

adapters.summary: Local endpoint implementing the AWS container-credentials protocol for components granted access through SF-027; upstream exchange with the AWS IoT credentials provider (X.509 thing certificate plus role alias) or IAM Roles Anywhere.
aws_services: AWS IoT credentials provider (credentials.iot.<region>.amazonaws.com:443) or IAM Roles Anywhere
adapters.auth: Upstream: an explicitly configured, separately provisioned AWS X.509 certificate and key (IoT thing certificate plus role alias, or an IAM Roles Anywhere certificate). This is a separate trust domain from the Sui device signer and Seal identity: SF-021 and SF-053 protect the Sui key and create no AWS certificate. The AWS key may be held through SF-021 hardware signer support or delivered through SF-022 when protected distribution is selected; mock-backed implementation uses a local CA. Local: a per-component bearer token in AWS_CONTAINER_AUTHORIZATION_TOKEN, deny by default through SF-027 grants. Credentials stay in memory and never reach chain, Walrus, journals or logs.
adapters.licensing: Clean-room implementation of the documented container-credentials protocol. No AWS closed-source component code. AWS SDKs used by tests are Apache-2.0.

runtime_tests: Run credential-provider-cases.json against the real adapter process
Unmodified boto3 and AWS SDK for Rust clients inside supervised components resolve credentials from AWS_CONTAINER_CREDENTIALS_FULL_URI/AWS_CONTAINER_AUTHORIZATION_TOKEN
Ungranted components receive neither variable; foreign, missing and revoked tokens are refused
Mutual-TLS exchange against a local mock credentials-provider endpoint, including expiry refresh, client/server/unknown error backoff and serving unexpired cached credentials
Daemon and component restart issue fresh tokens; no credential material is written to disk
acceptance.environment: Network-none container with a local mock credentials endpoint and CA
deferred: Real AWS account role-alias exchange; needs separate user authorization for an AWS account (unrun)

adapters.summary: SF-034 stream export destinations for Kinesis Data Streams (PutRecords) and Amazon S3 (multipart PutObject), using credential-provider and the SF-034 idempotent checkpoints.
adapters.auth: SF-057 container credentials; Kinesis PutRecords on the selected stream; S3 PutObject/GetObject/AbortMultipartUpload on an exclusive prefix and ListBucketMultipartUploads for exact-key crash cleanup. Provision IAM/KMS separately.
adapters.licensing: Clean-room Python companion using the existing Apache-2.0 boto3/botocore SDK from SF-057. Stream manager's SDK wire protocol is not reproduced.

runtime_tests: Export checkpoint sequence outcomes from stream-cases.json hold across exporter crash and restart (no unexported records skipped, monotonic checkpoints; crash-reserved sequence gaps explicitly reported)
Unmodified boto3 reads back exactly the exported records from a local Kinesis/S3 emulator (moto server, Apache-2.0)
Throttling, 5xx and expired-credential responses retry with backoff and never advance the checkpoint
Bandwidth limit and multipart minimum part size are enforced
acceptance.environment: Network-none container with a local AWS API emulator
deferred: Real AWS account Kinesis/S3 export; needs separate user authorization (unrun)

adapters.summary: Exports SF-019 native metrics and component-published metric requests to CloudWatch PutMetricData with a bounded retention buffer and publish interval.
adapters.auth: credential-provider credentials; the device role needs cloudwatch:PutMetricData. Components publish only on topics granted by SF-027.
adapters.licensing: Clean-room implementation. The AWS component is released under the Greengrass Core Software License Agreement and is not reused.

runtime_tests: Run cloudwatch-metrics-cases.json against the real adapter, with upstream results injected by a local CloudWatch emulator
Metrics from SF-019 and from a granted component reach the emulator with the configured namespace, dimensions (plus coreName), unit and timestamp, at most 20 per PutMetricData call
Publish-interval batching, the 20-metric namespace trigger, same-namespace retention replacement (counted drops, never silent) and buffering across daemon restart
Ungranted publishers and malformed metric requests are rejected with a status message on cloudwatch/metric/put/status
acceptance.environment: Network-none container with a local AWS API emulator
deferred: Real AWS account metrics; needs separate user authorization (unrun)

adapters.summary: Uploads SF-020 collected component and system logs to CloudWatch Logs with per-source retention, redaction and bounded local spool.
adapters.auth: credential-provider credentials; the device role needs logs:CreateLogGroup, logs:CreateLogStream and logs:PutLogEvents on the configured groups only.
adapters.licensing: Clean-room implementation using the Apache-2.0 AWS SDK for Rust.

runtime_tests: Run cloudwatch-logs-cases.json against the real adapter, with upstream results injected by a local CloudWatch Logs emulator
Log lines from a supervised component and the journal arrive in chronological order in the emulator under the LogManager 2.3.14 group and stream names
Redaction removes configured secrets before spooling; key and token material never appears in the spool or upload

Spool limit with counted oldest-first drops (a line larger than the whole spool drops only itself), offline catch-up, and restart without lost batches; a batch whose response was lost is resent unchanged (at least once)

Batches respect the PutLogEvents 10,000-event, 1,048,576-byte and single-day limits; lines over 256 KiB are split at UTF-8 character boundaries as LogManager 2.2.2 and later do, so no event or batch exceeds a limit
acceptance.environment: Network-none container with a local AWS API emulator
deferred: Real AWS account log upload; needs separate user authorization (unrun)

adapters.summary: One MQTT 3.1.1/5 TLS connection from the device to AWS IoT Core as an AWS IoT thing. It would serve the SF-032 IotCore bridge target, SF-033 cloud shadow sync, Device Defender and tunnel notifications.
aws_services: AWS IoT Core data endpoint (port 8883 or 443 with ALPN)
adapters.auth: An explicitly configured, separately provisioned AWS IoT thing certificate, key, policy and endpoint; a separate trust domain from the Sui device identity. The key may be held through SF-021 hardware signer support.
adapters.licensing: Clean-room MQTT client; no AWS component code.

runtime_tests: Bridge IotCore mappings deliver QoS 1 at least once through disconnects against a local MQTT broker with AWS-style mutual TLS
Shadow sync conflict policy applies to concurrent local and cloud updates
Unauthorized identities and topics are refused; reconnect after outage and certificate rotation recover
acceptance.environment: Network-none container with a local TLS MQTT broker
deferred: Real AWS IoT Core endpoint; needs separate user authorization (unrun)

adapters.specification_gap: SF-061 must pin the Bridge and ShadowManager versions it matches and add an executable reference suite for the IotCore connection, rotation and cloud shadow synchronization.

adapters.summary: Publishes Device Defender device-side metrics to $aws/things/{thing}/defender/metrics/json at the AWS minimum 300-second interval through aws-iot-core-connection. The AWS server-side Detect service is not replicated locally.
adapters.licensing: Clean-room implementation; the AWS component is under the Greengrass Core Software License Agreement.

runtime_tests: Published metric reports validate against the AWS Device Defender device-side metrics JSON schema; sample interval and retry count limits are enforced
Accepted and rejected responses are handled; reports are buffered and retried while disconnected
acceptance.environment: Network-none container with a local TLS MQTT broker
deferred: Real AWS IoT Device Defender account; needs separate user authorization (unrun)

adapters.specification_gap: SF-062 must add an executable schema/topic reference suite pinned to the Device Defender device-side metrics schema.

adapters.summary: An explicitly enabled, supervised component that starts the Apache-2.0 AWS IoT secure tunneling local proxy in destination mode on $aws/things/+/tunnels/notify, only for allow-listed local services. It coexists with platform-owned SSH daemon, firewall and service configuration, which it neither manages nor replaces; it runs no arbitrary remote commands and triggers no platform reboot.
adapters.auth: aws-iot-core-connection thing identity; the ephemeral per-tunnel client access token arrives in the notification and is never logged or journaled.
adapters.licensing: AWS IoT Secure Tunneling Local Proxy is Apache-2.0; it needs OpenSSL 3 and glibc 2.35 or later in the image.

runtime_tests: Tunnel notifications start at most maxConcurrentTunnels proxies, only for allow-listed services, and stop at tunnelTimeoutSeconds
Denied destinations and callers are refused, tokens never leak to logs or other processes, and proxies are cleaned up after connection failures or component replacement
acceptance.environment: Network-none container with a local TLS MQTT broker and a stub tunnel endpoint
deferred: Real AWS IoT secure tunnel; needs separate user authorization (unrun)

adapters.specification_gap: SF-063 must add an executable notification/destination reference suite.

platform_phases.reason: Initial prototype phase; development host target.
Initial prototype phase; Yocto and Raspberry Pi target.
Initial prototype phase; 32-bit ARM catalog selection.

Native i686 daemon, release bundle and x86 catalog selection exist (SF-076, docs/LINUX_X86.md), but managed adapters do not target it and translation omits and reports x86 manifests. A tracked gap, not an approved exclusion.

Native Windows SCM/Job Object local executable runtime exists (SF-074, docs/WINDOWS_RUNTIME.md); SID/ACL and interrupted-lifecycle software evidence is separate from reference vectors. Catalog/chain/rich IPC and managed adapters remain unsupported. Translation still omits Windows manifests; remaining full-parity work stays tracked by SF-064.

The native macOS runtime (SF-075, docs/MACOS_RUNTIME.md) runs SuiFleet components; AWS lists only Linux and Windows for the components in this catalog, so their macOS equivalents remain a tracked gap, not an approved exclusion.
